ruleName: Ball Lifted or Deliberately Touched by Player or Causes It to Move
imagePrompt: Illustrate a semi-realistic golf scene on a sunlit fairway. Show a golfer in the act of a practice swing with a divot flying forward, just about to strike or just striking a nearby golf ball and making it move. The moment should focus on the connection between the divot and the ball. Ensure the golfer, the flying divot, and the ball's position are clearly visible. The scene should have a polished, modern look, about 75% realistic and 25% stylised, with good depth and lighting. Do not include any text, labels, arrows, numbers, diagrams, badges, logos, watermarks, club crests, scorecards or speech bubbles.
imageAlt: A golfer on the fairway takes a practice swing, and the flying divot is about to hit a golf ball, causing the ball to move.

sceneSpec.setting: Short mown fairway, with green grass and a clear view of the fairway area.
sceneSpec.players: One golfer, mid-practice swing, with a golf club in hand. The golfer is visible to the side of the scene, showing a follow-through after the practice swing.
sceneSpec.ballPosition: Golf ball originally at rest on the fairway, a short distance ahead.
sceneSpec.ruleMoment: The divot taken by the practice swing is depicted in the air, just moments before or as it makes contact with the ball, which has just started to move.
sceneSpec.educationalFocus: The effect of a player's own actions, even indirect, moving the ball during a practice swing.
mustShow: A flying divot in motion from a player's practice swing
Golfer clearly shown in mid-practice swing
mustNotShow: Diagrams, badges, logos, watermarks, or club crests

questions.title: Practice Swing Makes Your Ball Move
questions.question: Your ball is on the short grass. You take a practice swing, and your club makes a chunk of grass fly. The flying grass hits your ball and makes it roll away. What should you do?

choices.text: No penalty, because you did not hit the ball with your club.
No penalty. Hit the ball from where it rolled to.
You get one penalty shot because your practice swing made the ball move. Put the ball back where it was.

questions.explanation: Even though you did not hit the ball with your club, your practice swing made grass move your ball. That means you have to add one penalty shot. You must put the ball back where it was before you play your next shot.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: A piece of grass and dirt that your club may cut out of the ground during a swing.
Extra shots added to your score because you broke a rule.
Put the ball back in the spot it was before it moved.

questions.teachingTip: Show children how practice swings can move grass and remind them to check their ball after practising near it.
likelyMisconceptions: Thinking you only get a penalty if you hit the ball with your club.
Thinking you can just play the ball from where it rolled to after any practice swing.

questions.title: Practice Swing Moves Your Ball
questions.question: Your ball lies on the fairway. Before playing your shot, you take a practice swing and accidentally take a divot. The divot flies forward, hits your ball and causes it to move. What is the correct ruling?

choices.text: There is no penalty because you did not touch the ball with your club.
There is no penalty. Play the ball from its new position.
You receive a one-stroke penalty because your actions caused the ball to move. You must replace the ball on its original spot.

questions.explanation: Although the club did not touch the ball, your practice swing caused the divot to move the ball. As your action is responsible for the ball's movement, you receive a one-stroke penalty and must replace the ball on its original spot before making your next stroke. This is covered under Rule 9.4.
